USE CASES

Where this pays off in a jewellery business.

Four everyday situations, and what changes when Jwero handles them.

01

Diamond parcels need to be tracked by carat as stones are drawn out.

Stone lots hold carat and count balances, and single stones can be split out and tracked with certificates.

What changesParcel balances stay right after every draw.

02

Jewellers take diamonds on memo and return some weeks later.

Issue on memo to each buyer, then close lines as sold or returned.

What changesMemo stock is never mixed up with sold stock.

03

You show stock at a trade exhibition and need every piece back.

Create an exhibition, send stock to it, and check every piece back or sold.

What changesNothing goes missing between the show and the office.

04

A buyer asks for stones by size and quality.

Search lots and stones by grade, size and certificate number.

What changesQuotes start from real stock, not memory.

IF YOU TRADE STONES, NOT JEWELLERY

What a diamond trader gets today, and what is still on the roadmap.

Traders work certificate-first, memo-heavy and across borders. Here is the honest split.

Certificate-first records

Each stone carries its GIA/IGI number, shape, carat, colour, clarity and cut on the catalogue, the certificate is the identity, not an afterthought.

Memo to many buyers

Stones out on memo or consignment to several buyers at once, each with a return date, so exposure per counterparty is visible.

Buyer-tiered prices, multi-currency

Private price lists per buyer, invoices in the currency the buyer pays in.

Deals on the channel buyers use

WhatsApp catalogues, quotes and follow-ups on the thread where the deal is actually done.

WHAT WE DON'T DO YET

Here's what's on the public roadmap, not the product, said plainly, before you find out the hard way.

  • Parcel-as-lot accounting in carats with a price per carat, today a parcel is entered as its stones, not as one lot.
  • Discount-off-list (Rapaport-style) pricing, pricing is per stone or per buyer list, not a percentage off a published sheet.
  • Export documentation for cross-border shipments is not generated in Jwero.
See the full public roadmap →

QUESTIONS DIAMOND WHOLESALERS ASK

Memo tracking, pricing and trust: answered.

Can I share different prices with different buyers?

Yes, buyer-tiered pricing and catalogue visibility are configurable, so each buyer sees their own terms.

Can memo and approval status be tracked per stone?

Order and pipeline tracking hold memo and approval status per item, replacing the register-hunting that comes with paper memos.

I trade loose diamonds and parcels, not jewellery. Is this for me?

Partly, and we would rather say where the line is. Today Jwero holds each stone with its certificate number, shape, carat, colour, clarity and cut on the catalogue; tracks it out on memo and consignment to several buyers with return dates; prices per buyer with tiered lists; and invoices in more than one currency. What it does not do yet is treat a parcel as a lot in carats with a price per carat, or price as a discount off a list, those are on the roadmap, and until they ship a trader who works parcel-by-parcel will still keep that sheet outside Jwero.

Our buyer relationships run on trust built over years. Won’t a system feel transactional?

The system holds the record; your team still holds the relationship. It replaces the register-hunting, not the trust, the buyer still deals with a person, just one who has the memo history in front of them.

More questions jewellers ask.

Can stones be searched by certificate number?

Yes. Each stone drawn from a parcel can be searched by certificate, barcode or tag. Each stone keeps its own record, including where it is now and which parcel it came from.

Can I merge returned stones back into a parcel?

Lots can be split today. Merging returned stones back into a parent lot is not available yet. Returned stones can still be recorded as their own lot, and their carats are tracked, but they stay separate from the original parcel.

Do you handle stones held for another supplier?

Yes. Consignment agreements keep a supplier's goods apart from your own until sold. Each agreement lists the supplier's stones, you pay only for what you sell, and the rest goes back on record.
